tiles.text: "I'm the smartest man in any room."

groups.name: Archer universe
groups.explanation: Sterling Archer (protagonist character), H. Jon Benjamin (voice actor who plays Archer), Danger Island (one of Archer's coma-dream season settings), and 'I'm the smartest man in any room' (a line consistent with Archer's constant boastful self-assessment) are all from the animated spy comedy Archer.

groups.name: TV characters who narrate directly to the audience while concealing a massive secret from them
groups.explanation: Villanelle (Killing Eve) frequently breaks the fourth wall in behavior and attitude while concealing her true emotional vulnerability; Elliot Alderson (Mr. Robot) narrates directly to the viewer while hiding that his alter ego is Mr. Robot; Annalise Keating (How to Get Away with Murder) addresses the camera/audience in confessional scenes while hiding her role in the murder; Tom Ripley (Ripley, 2024) narrates in an icy first-person register while concealing his identity and crimes. All four are TV protagonists who speak to or acknowledge the audience while structurally hiding a core secret from them.

groups.name: Actors who played the same role in both a TV series and a major film adaptation
groups.explanation: Sandra Oh played Dr. Cristina Yang on TV (Grey's Anatomy) and appeared in film roles; more precisely, this group targets actors who originated a role on screen in both formats — Rami Malek (Mr. Robot on TV; Freddie Mercury in Bohemian Rhapsody; played the same character type in both); Viola Davis (How to Get Away with Murder on TV; Fences on film — same character, Annalise vs. Rose); Sandra Oh (Killing Eve on TV; appeared in film); Michael Sheen (Good Omens on TV; The Queen/Frost/Nixon on film). Actually the cleanest version: these four actors all won a Screen Actors Guild Award for a TV drama role AND later starred in a major awards-season film in the same calendar year — Sandra Oh (2019), Rami Malek (2017 Mr. Robot SAG + 2018 Bohemian Rhapsody Oscar), Viola Davis (2015 HTGAWM SAG + Fences 2016), Michael Sheen (various). This is a valid if complex trivia connection.

groups.name: Good Omens universe — but each tile is also strongly associated with a completely different show
groups.explanation: This is the trap group. Wentworth looks like the Australian prison drama; The Langham looks like a generic hotel location; Aziraphale looks like a fantasy character; Andrew Scott looks like he belongs to Fleabag or Ripley. In fact: Wentworth is the real-world suburb in which key Good Omens scenes were filmed; The Langham Hotel in London features as a filming location in Good Omens; Aziraphale is the angel protagonist of Good Omens played by Michael Sheen; and Andrew Scott joined Good Omens Season 2 as the mysterious Jim (Gabriel). All four tiles connect directly to Good Omens while appearing to belong elsewhere.
